text: Before his usual meeting with Beatrice, Giovanni bought fresh flowers, but they drooped in his hand, and when he breathed upon a spider on the ceiling, it shuddered and hung lifeless. <break time="0.8s" /> Horrified to discover that he, too, carried the poison of the garden, he rushed down to Beatrice and cried, Accursed one, you have made me as hateful and deadly as yourself. <break time="0.8s" /> Beatrice, pale with grief, answered that she had never wished it, and told him how her father had raised her alongside the shrub, which had sprung from his science at the very hour of her birth. <break time="0.8s" /> Softened at last, Giovanni held out Baglionis antidote and proposed that they drink it together, but she took it from him, saying, I will drink, but do you await the result. <break time="0.8s" /> At that moment Rappaccini appeared and, spreading his hands over them like a father blessing his children, declared in triumph that his daughter need no longer be lonely in the world. <break time="0.8s" /> Why did you inflict this miserable doom upon your child, Beatrice asked faintly, and when he replied that he had freed her from the weakness of ordinary women, she said she would rather have been loved than feared. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, turning to Giovanni, she sighed, Oh, was there not, from the first, more poison in thy nature than in mine, and since poison had been her life, the antidote became her death. <break time="0.8s" /> So she passed away at the feet of her father and Giovanni, and Baglioni, looking down from the window, called out in a tone of triumph mixed with horror, Rappaccini, Rappaccini, And is this the upshot of your experiment.
